ffa617857253dbecc3a5371f478e33e4b1625baa.summary: Trend Micro blog timeline of the Sandworm vulnerability, CVE-2014-4114, a command injection flaw in the Windows OLE component. The report links the flaw to a PowerPoint (PPSX) email campaign from August 2014 attributed to Sandworm, also called BlackEnergy. It traces public disclosure by iSIGHT on October 14, 2014, the same-day Microsoft fix in MS14-060, the bypass disclosed on October 21 as CVE-2014-6352, and the same technique used against SCADA systems. It says the technique dates to at least October 2013 and explains how the flaw bypasses Mark of the Web protection.
